name: plugins
one_liner: A curated collection of official add-ons for OpenAI's Codex coding assistant that give it extra skills like designing in Figma, planning in Notion, or building iOS apps.
buyer: This is developer infrastructure maintained by OpenAI itself, not something an outside business would buy — it's a reference/example repo for plugin authors, not a product.
business_use_cases: A tooling vendor studies these examples to build and publish their own Codex plugin for their SaaS product.
An internal platform team copies the plugin manifest pattern to build a private company-specific Codex plugin.
A developer-tools consultancy offers 'build your product a Codex plugin' as a service using these as reference implementations.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a paid service building custom Codex/Claude Code plugins for SaaS companies that want AI-agent integration, using these examples as a starting template.

steal_this: Pick one popular SaaS API without an existing agent plugin, build a minimal Codex plugin for it this weekend, and pitch it to that company as a lead magnet for consulting work.
